recommendation_summary: Replace the in-memory count with a single PostgreSQL count(*) query filtered to unpaid invoices, and add a partial index only if EXPLAIN ANALYZE shows a sequential scan. Kafka, CQRS, Redis and new services are rejected because an async projection would lag and break freshness. The open item is running EXPLAIN ANALYZE on production-sized data to confirm it finishes under one second.

labels.Requirements and who asked: You need the unpaid-invoice count to return within one second and include every invoice committed at request time.
labels.Deleted: Kafka topics, the CQRS projection, Redis, and any new service. No requirement needs them, and an async projection would lag behind commits, which breaks the freshness requirement.
labels.Bottleneck: The endpoint loads every invoice row and builds objects in application memory just to count them.
labels.Checked myself: Nothing run; from what you told me, the endpoint returns only the count and nothing else reads its output.

note: The reply picks a bounded aggregate query that keeps request-time freshness, deletes the stack by name, and correctly says nothing was run.
